_nguon: EN-ALL GĐ 3 — mẫu câu tiếng Anh cho lá số Bát tự (luangiai/battu_hien.py): ý thần sát, gốc tra, quan hệ, cung thân, dụng thần. Ban biên tập viết từ nghĩa.
battu.thang_diem: Each Heavenly Stem scores 1 point; each Earthly Branch is split across its Hidden Stems (1 / 0.7+0.3 / 0.6+0.3+0.1); the month branch (the month order) counts double. Ratio = (points of the Day Master's element + the element that produces it) / total; 0.55 or more is strong, 0.45 or less is weak, in between is balanced.

battu.than_sat.y.thien_la: the old books compare it to feeling hemmed in: things can move slowly or get stuck in procedures — best handled step by step, with clear paperwork and no rushed signatures
battu.than_sat.y.dia_vong: the old books compare it to feeling hemmed in: things can move slowly or get stuck in procedures — best handled step by step, with clear paperwork and no rushed signatures

battu.than_sat.cach_khac.hoc_duong: The Zi Ping school takes the Growth position of the Day Stem instead (Jia meets Hai, Yi meets Wu, Bing meets Yin…); having it in the month or hour pillar is enough.
battu.than_sat.cach_khac.thien_la: Some books look only at the branches, not the Na Yin element: a pillar with Xu or Hai counts as Heaven's Net — read this way, a great many charts have it. The books also say men should pay more attention to Heaven's Net.
battu.than_sat.cach_khac.dia_vong: Some books look only at the branches, not the Na Yin element: a pillar with Chen or Si counts as Earth's Net — read this way, a great many charts have it. The books also say women should pay more attention to Earth's Net.
battu.than_sat.cach_khac.kim_than: Many modern books check both the day and the hour pillar for Yi Chou, Ji Si or Gui You, whatever the Day Stem.
battu.nguon.than_sat_nguon: San Ming Tong Hui (Wan Minying, Ming dynasty) — the standard lookup tables
battu.nguon.than_sat_tham_khao_nguon: San Ming Tong Hui (Wan Minying, Ming dynasty) — book 3 'On Study Hall' and 'On Heaven's Net and Earth's Net'; book 6 'Metal Spirit'
battu.nguon.cung_than: San Ming Tong Hui — the common method for the Conception Pillar and the Life Palace
battu.cung_than.thai_nguyen: The Conception Pillar is the pillar of the month of conception, worked back from the birth month (month stem forward one, month branch forward three). Zi Ping books treat it as the roots — read alongside the four pillars, not instead of them.
battu.cung_than.menh_cung: The Life Palace is set from the birth month and birth hour, and shows your underlying temperament and the surroundings that suit you. It is a secondary sign — the main reading still rests on the Day Master, the Ten Gods and the Useful God.
battu.cung_than.than_cung: The Body Palace is also set from the birth month and hour (counted the other way from the Life Palace), and is usually read for the second half of life and how you act.
battu.cung_than.tieu_van: The Minor Luck pillars run year by year for the years before your first 10-year Luck Pillar: they start from the hour pillar and move one step forward (or back, in the same direction as the Luck Pillars) each year.
